title: Anomalous Frequency Shift in Low-Loss Superconducting Granular Aluminum Resonators
authors: Patrick Winkel, Daniil S. Antonenko, Vishakha Gupta, Neel Thakur, Pavel Kurilovich, Luigi Frunzio, Leonid I. Glazman, Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract: Superconducting high-kinetic inductance materials like granular aluminum (grAl) are a versatile part of the circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) toolbox, provided their losses at microwave frequencies are low enough. To further advance the use of grAl in quantum devices, it is indispensable to identify the dominant loss mechanisms. The standard approach pairs electromagnetic simulations of resonator geometry with measured temperature and power dependence of resonance frequency and loss rate. Most materials follow the phenomenological theory of two-level systems (TLSs) at low temperatures, resulting in an initial decrease of the resonance frequency with increasing temperature. In our work, we observe an opposite behavior at the lowest temperatures: The resonance frequency initially increases with both temperature and readout power, contradicting the standard TLS model predictions. We are able to explain a part of the data by an alternative mechanism associated with the effect of superconducting quasiparticles in a granular system with spatially-nonuniform gap. Yet, the observed change in the resonance frequency with temperature is not matched by a proportional change in the loss rate. We also observe anomalous positive frequency responses following high-energy events, characterized by several time scales. While anomalous behavior has been reported previously in grAl, the disagreement with standard models is particularly visible in our devices thanks to their exceptionally low loss rates.
summary: This work investigates anomalous frequency shifts in superconducting granular aluminum resonators, finding that the frequency initially increases with temperature and power at low temperatures, contrary to standard TLS predictions. The authors propose a quasiparticle mechanism related to the granular structure to explain this anomaly. The findings are crucial for advancing superconducting circuits in quantum technology by pinpointing fundamental loss mechanisms.
main_problem: The primary goal is to identify the dominant loss mechanisms and explain the anomalous frequency shifts observed in low-loss superconducting granular aluminum (grAl) resonators.
main_result: The resonance frequency exhibits an initial positive shift with increasing temperature and power at low T, contradicting standard Two-Level System (TLS) predictions, which can partially be explained by superconducting quasiparticle effects in a granular system.
method: The study involves characterizing the complex admittance by measuring the resonance frequency and loss rate as functions of temperature and input power in the single-photon regime.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting resonator made from granular aluminum (grAl). Theoretical models considered include the TLS model and an alternative model treating grAl as an array of superconducting grains with spatially non-uniform superconducting gaps.
key_observables: Resonance frequency shift ($\Delta f$), internal loss rate ($1/Q_i$), and their dependence on temperature ($T$) and readout power ($P_{in}$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to $\sim 100$ mK), single-photon regime ($ ar{n} \approx 1$), and the superconducting gap structure.
main_assumptions: The standard TLS model is assumed to be insufficient for describing the low-temperature frequency dependence, and the quasiparticle model is used to explain the initial anomalous behavior.
figures_summary: Figures show the temperature dependence of frequency and loss, the power dependence of frequency shift, and the time dynamics of frequency following high-energy events.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements showing deviations from standard models (TLS), proposes a quasiparticle mechanism to explain the low-T anomalies, and discusses limitations regarding the loss rate and high-energy response.
why_interesting: The anomalous electrodynamics observed in superconducting resonators, particularly the deviation from standard TLS predictions, touches upon non-equilibrium dynamics and quasiparticle physics relevant to open quantum systems.
